title: Packaging verifiable billing evidence for SOC compliance and customer audits
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: produce an audit-ready evidence package and export surface for billing/metering, quotas, and rate-limiting that satisfies SOC-style evidence requests and supports customer forensic queries. Deliverables: 1) deterministic, signed billing run exports (per-customer, per-period) with raw event provenance; 2) tamper-evident append-only billing logs with retention policies and access controls; 3) queryable snapshots and a compact evidence bundle format for SOC/third-party auditors; 4) operator playbook for responding to audit requests and reproducing billed quantities. The work spans runtime instrumentation (token accounting, batch attribution), backend aggregation pipelines, storage/retention, RBAC for evidence access, and console/UI endpoints for packaging and download.
acceptance_criteria: Signed billing run export available for a specified customer and month which includes raw request ids, timestamped metering events, model variant used, token counts, applied quotas and rate-limit events, and final billed units.
Export package contains a manifest + cryptographic signature (Ed25519) and a reproducibility script that re-aggregates totals from raw events to match the exported summary.
Append-only billing log is write-once (immutable) with retention policy configurable per-customer and audit trail showing who/when accessed export bundles.
RBAC enforced: only users with 'billing:auditor' role or explicit request approval can access PII-containing export bundles; access is logged and retained for 2 years.
Playbook documenting steps to handle an external auditor request within SLA (72 hours) with templated evidence bundle, checklist, and point-of-contact.
End-to-end tests that simulate rate-limit and quota events and verify they are recorded, aggregated, and surfaced in the export with matching signatures.
decisions: Use Ed25519 for signing export manifests to balance implementation complexity and strong non-repudiation.
Store raw billing events in S3 with object-immutable mode + periodic merkle-root summaries in the DB to provide tamper-evidence while keeping query performance acceptable.
Export format: newline-delimited JSON for raw events plus a compressed (gz) manifest and signature so auditors can stream-verify records.
Keep retention defaults at 2 years for audit evidence but allow enterprise customers to opt into longer retention via contract (billing-privacy team to own billing tier mapping).

risks: PII leakage risk if export packaging step misses cleanup; mitigation: explicit scrub policy and automated lint check failing export when PII fields present unless flagged.
Performance impact of signing large exports during peak: mitigation via asynchronous signing and background worker with throttling and priority queue for audit requests.
Regulatory: different regions require different retention minima; mitigation: policy mapping table and region-aware retention enforcement.
